Container.Name: openviking
Container.Overview:
OpenViking is an open-source context database for AI agents by Volcengine. It stores memories, resources and skills in a file-system-like hierarchy (viking:// URIs) with tiered loading, semantic retrieval and automatic session memory. It is used by agents such as OpenClaw, Claude Code and Codex through its HTTP API, CLI, MCP server and SDKs.
**What runs in the container**
- The OpenViking HTTP API on port 1933, which also serves the **Web Studio** UI at `/studio` - The bundled VikingBot gateway (disable with Enable VikingBot = false) - Health check: `http://YOUR-SERVER-IP:1933/health` - Optional OpenViking LLM Gateway under `/gateway`: enable it in Studio (OpenViking Gateway page) or add a variable `OPENVIKING_GATEWAY_ENABLED=true`
**First run: create ov.conf**
All state lives in one folder mapped to `/app/.openviking`: `ov.conf`, `ovcli.conf` and the workspace (`./data` resolves to `/app/.openviking/data`). If `ov.conf` is missing, the container waits and answers every request with a 503 explaining what to do. Pick one:
1. Run the wizard: `docker exec -it openviking openviking-server init`. The server starts by itself once the file exists. 2. Or create `/mnt/user/appdata/openviking/ov.conf` yourself before starting. Minimal example:
`{` ` "server": { "root_api_key": "CHANGE-ME-long-random-string" },` ` "storage": { "workspace": "./data" },` ` "embedding": { "dense": { "provider": "openai", "api_base": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api_key": "sk-...", "model": "text-embedding-3-large", "dimension": 3072 } },` ` "vlm": { "provider": "openai", "api_base": "https://api.openai.com/v1", "api_key": "sk-...", "model": "gpt-4o-mini" }` `}`
Because the server listens on 0.0.0.0 inside Docker, `server.root_api_key` (or another auth mode) is **required**, otherwise OpenViking refuses to start. The root key is an admin credential; create user keys for agents and for VikingBot (`bot.ov_server.api_key`). Providers such as Ollama, vLLM, Gemini, Volcengine and LiteLLM are supported; see the configuration guide.
**Upgrading from an older template** (config at /app/ov.conf, data at /app/data): stop the container, move `ov.conf` into the new config folder, and move the old data folder to `/mnt/user/appdata/openviking/data` (keeping workspace `./data`), or keep an absolute workspace path and map it with an extra Path. The old port 8020 console was replaced by Web Studio at `/studio` on port 1933.
Docs: https://github.com/volcengine/OpenViking/tree/main/docs/en

Container.Requires: An ov.conf with server.root_api_key plus an embedding model and a VLM (OpenAI-compatible, Ollama, Gemini, Volcengine and more)
Container.Changes: ### 2026-11-22 - Moved config and data to the single /app/.openviking folder used by current images (see the upgrade note) - Removed the openviking-server post argument so the entrypoint's first-run handling, host binding and VikingBot start work again - WebUI now opens Web Studio on port 1933 (/studio); the 8020 console no longer exists - Added ov.conf bootstrap, server host/port and public base URL variables, and documented the gateway - Added the template URL and fixed the registry link ### 2026-04-10 - Fixed XML formatting and the VikingBot setting ### 2026-04-09 - Initial release

Config.Name: API / Web Studio Port
Config.Description: OpenViking HTTP API, MCP and Web Studio (/studio). Must match Server Port if you change it.

Config.Name: Config and Data
Config.Description: Holds ov.conf, ovcli.conf and the default workspace (data/). Create ov.conf here or run openviking-server init.

Config.Name: Enable VikingBot
Config.Description: 1 starts the bundled VikingBot gateway with the server. Set 0 for a server-only deployment. VikingBot needs a user/admin key in bot.ov_server.api_key.

Config.Name: ov.conf Content (first run)
Config.Description: Optional. Full ov.conf JSON on one line. Written to /app/.openviking/ov.conf only if that file does not exist yet. You can clear it after the first start.

Config.Name: Server Host
Config.Description: Bind address inside the container. Keep 0.0.0.0 for Docker port mapping.

Config.Name: Server Port
Config.Description: Port inside the container. Overrides server.port in ov.conf; change the port mapping too if you change this.

Config.Name: Public Base URL
Config.Description: Public HTTPS URL when exposed through a reverse proxy, e.g. https://ov.example.com (needed for OAuth and internet MCP clients).

Config.Name: Startup Health Attempts
Config.Description: Seconds the entrypoint waits for the server to become healthy before giving up.
